title: Coupled Resonator Filter - Band 38 (2600 MHz TDD) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Coupled Resonator Filter filter targeting Band 38 (2600 MHz TDD) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on 42° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 4825.5 MHz and bandwidth of 341.2 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Coupled Resonator Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 38 (2600 MHz TDD)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: 42° YX LiTaO3
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: Keysight ADS 2024
- Design Center: Newbury Park Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Coupled Resonator Filter design targeting Band 38 (2600 MHz TDD). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4825.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       341.2 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 19.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 44.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 45.0 dB
Q Factor:               13201
Temperature Coefficient:-28.9 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.8 x 1.0 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   7
Electrode Material:     Mo/Al
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Keysight ADS 2024 and load the Coupled Resonator Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 42° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4825.5 MHz, BW 341.2 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 42° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 14476 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 19.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 512 MHz offset >= 44.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 17.4 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 85%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-10-08
Devices Tested:         70
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.13 dB
Return Loss (meas):     20.6 dB
Rejection (meas):       46.7 dB
Isolation (meas):       49.8 dB
Q Factor (meas):        13201
Group Delay Variation:  2.0 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              97.7%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Coupled Resonator Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 38 (2600 MHz TDD).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Batch-to-batch reproducibility confirmed over 3 wafer lots.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
